q7.answer: Workers learn the mode from the billing_mode flag in the config service, but the durable rollout record is the authority during a rollback. Workers check the record before every charge, so a worker with a stale flag still stops. An invoice in flight is protected by the idempotency key (customer plus billing period), which the ledger enforces as unique and the payment provider receives, so a stale worker or retry cannot charge it twice. During a rollback, Freeze stops new-engine charges and queues any that fall due. I did not specify finer-grained handling of a half-computed invoice beyond that.

q8.answer: The evidence is in the durable rollout record next to the ledger. It holds the G1 and G2 counters, and the nightly comparison job produces the data behind them. The job reports a gate as met, but a person makes the move. Every change is a compare-and-set on the record's version, and the controller accepts a forward move only when the gate is met. G2 also needs Finance sign-off and the usage events pinned. Forward moves are also refused while a rollback is in progress.

q9.answer: The rollout controller evaluates the condition every minute over a sliding 10-minute window. It measures failed charge attempts divided by all charge attempts, counting system failures such as timeouts, provider errors and our own errors, and excluding ordinary card declines. It fires when the rate is above 2% with at least 10 system failures, and only in both or new_only before rollback_closed_at. When it fires, it starts an automatic Rollback through the same compare-and-set as a manual start. Below the 10-failure minimum it only pages on-call. The 10-failure minimum is a proposed default (open question 1).

q10.answer: Freeze stops the new engine from charging immediately, and charges that fall due are queued, not dropped. Nobody charges during the rollback. They are actually made at Switch, when billing_mode is set to old_only and the old engine resumes and charges only the queued periods. If the rollback goes to Blocked, the charges stay queued and billing is delayed until on-call resolves it.

q11.answer: Two things. First, Reconcile checks the ledger and the payment provider for each customer and period and classifies it as charged, not charged or in-flight. Charged periods are final and the old engine never touches them, and only not-charged periods are queued. Second, every charge carries an idempotency key made from customer and billing period. The ledger enforces uniqueness on the key and the provider receives it. If a period already has a new-engine ledger invoice that was not charged, that invoice stands and is never rewritten. If the outcome is unknown, the rollback goes to Blocked rather than guessing.

q12.answer: Billing is left frozen: the new engine is not charging, due charges are queued, and the flag is still unchanged until Switch. The rollback step is stored in the durable rollout record, so the next worker resumes from the recorded step, and every step is safe to repeat. A failed Reprocess batch is retried with backoff, up to 5 attempts. If retries are exhausted, events are missing, or the Reconcile outcome is unknown or the provider is unreachable, it goes to Blocked. Blocked pages on-call and escalates at 1 hour and 4 hours, with a 24-hour target, and has no automatic exit. On-call resolves it and the rollback resumes in the step where it stopped.
